en: a. relating to poetry or poets; expressing deep feelings in a beautiful way; having the qualities of poetry
ex: She described the sunset in a poetic way.
她用詩意的方式描寫日落。

en: n. a person who gives advice and help to people with personal problems; a person who helps students choose courses; a lawyer; a supervisor at a summer camp
ex: The school counselor helped him choose a university.
學校輔導員幫助他選擇大學。

en: n. a person who attacks and robs ships at sea; a person who copies and sells books, films or software illegally; vt. to copy and sell something without permission; vi. to attack and rob ships at sea
ex: The pirates attacked the merchant ship near the coast.
海盜在海岸附近襲擊了商船。

en: vi. to become an expert in one particular area of work or study; to limit your attention or activity to a particular subject; vt. to make something more specialized
ex: She decided to specialize in children's medicine.
她決定專攻兒科。
ph: a restaurant that specializes in seafood

en: n. a place that gives protection from danger or trouble; protection from danger; a safe place in the road for people to stand; vi. to take shelter; vt. to give someone a safe place
ex: The villagers took refuge in the church during the storm.
暴風雨期間，村民躲到教堂避難。

en: n. a group of people who sing together, especially in a church or school; the part of a church where such a group sits; v. to sing or speak together
ex: The school choir sang at the Christmas concert.
學校合唱團在聖誕音樂會上演唱。

en: n. a loan of money from a bank, used to buy a house, which you pay back over many years; a legal agreement to give someone the right to take your property if you do not pay back a loan; vt. to use property as a guarantee for a loan
ex: They took out a mortgage to buy their first home.
他們貸款買了第一棟房子。

en: a. relating to the work of managing a company, organization or institution; relating to the running of a government or an institution; connected with administration
ex: She works in an administrative position at the university.
她在大學擔任行政職務。

en: n. the force that pulls objects towards the center of the Earth; the seriousness of a situation; very serious behavior; a force that attracts objects toward one another
ex: The apple fell to the ground because of gravity.
蘋果因為重力而掉到地上。

en: n. the act of combining two or more things so they work together; the process of helping people to become part of a society; the act of combining two things into one
ex: The integration of immigrants takes time and effort.
移民的融入需要時間與努力。

en: a. clear and easy to see; plain; vt. to show something clearly; vi. to appear; n. a list of goods carried on a ship or plane, or of passengers
ex: His anger was manifest in the way he slammed the door.
他重重關門的樣子顯示出他的憤怒。

en: n. a long piece of writing on a subject, especially one that is part of a university degree; an idea or theory that someone puts forward and defends; a statement that a person tries to prove
ex: He is writing his master's thesis on climate change.
他正在寫關於氣候變遷的碩士論文。

en: n. the state of not having a job; the number of people without a job; the problem of people not having jobs
ex: The government is trying to reduce unemployment.
政府正努力降低失業率。

en: a. describing what something is like; giving a description of something; relating to the description of language rules as they are used
ex: The report includes a descriptive account of the experiment.
報告中包含對實驗的描述性說明。

en: n. a medical condition in which your body reacts badly to something that is normally harmless; a strong dislike for something; a medical sensitivity to a food or substance
ex: She has an allergy to peanuts and must be careful.
她對花生過敏，必須小心。

en: n. a doctor's written order for a medicine; an official order or rule; the act of giving an official order; something recommended as a way to achieve something
ex: The doctor wrote me a prescription for antibiotics.
醫生為我開了抗生素的處方。

en: n. an official statement or announcement; the act of stating something clearly in public; a written statement that you give to customs officers about goods you are carrying; a formal announcement of war
ex: The country issued a declaration of independence.
該國發布了獨立宣言。

en: n. a way of using words that are the opposite of what you mean in order to be funny or to criticize; a situation that is odd because it is the opposite of what you would expect; an amusing or sad contrast
ex: It is an irony that the fire station burned down.
諷刺的是，那間消防局竟然發生火災。

en: n. a professional cook who is in charge of a restaurant kitchen; a person who cooks food for a living; a person who is very good at cooking
ex: The chef prepared a special dish for the guests.
主廚為賓客準備了一道特別的菜餚。

en: n. an estimate of what might happen in the future based on the present situation; the act of showing a picture on a screen; a part that sticks out from a surface; the act of throwing something forward
ex: The sales projection for next year is encouraging.
明年的銷售預測令人鼓舞。

en: vt. to consist of particular parts or members; to make up a whole; to be formed from several parts
ex: The committee comprises ten members.
該委員會由十位成員組成。

en: vt. to break something into many pieces with force; to hit something very hard; to destroy something completely; vi. to break noisily; n. a loud sound of something breaking; a very successful performance; a hard hit in sports
ex: The children smashed the window with a ball.
孩子們用球打破了窗戶。

en: n. the act of putting a piece of equipment in position so that it is ready for use; a place where military equipment is located; a ceremony in which someone is officially put into a new job; a work of art installed in a gallery
ex: The installation of the new software took two hours.
新軟體的安裝花了兩小時。

en: n. a person who entertains an audience, such as an actor, musician or dancer; a person or thing that works or acts in a particular way; a person who performs a task
ex: The performers received a standing ovation.
表演者獲得了全場起立鼓掌。

en: n. money that is paid regularly to someone who has retired from work; a small hotel or guest house in Europe; vt. to pay someone a pension
ex: He receives a monthly pension from his former employer.
他每個月從前雇主那裡領取退休金。

en: n. a small amount or example of something used to represent the whole; an animal, plant or object used in scientific study; a particular example of a type of thing; a sample of blood or urine for testing
ex: The scientists collected a specimen of the rare plant.
科學家採集了那株稀有植物的標本。

en: n. a place where things are made or repaired by hand or with tools; a meeting or class where people learn or practice a particular skill; a small factory; a training session
ex: She attended a writing workshop last weekend.
她上週末參加了一場寫作工作坊。

en: vt. to produce or cause something to exist; to make energy or electricity; to cause a feeling or reaction; to produce something using a computer
ex: Wind turbines generate electricity from the wind.
風力渦輪機利用風力發電。

en: n. all the living things in an area and the way they affect each other and the environment; a community of plants and animals that interact with each other and their physical surroundings
ex: The pollution is damaging the delicate ecosystem of the lake.
污染正破壞這座湖脆弱的生態系統。

en: vt. to surprise and slightly frighten someone; to cause someone to jump suddenly; vi. to be suddenly frightened; n. a sudden surprise or fright
ex: The loud noise startled the baby.
巨大的聲響嚇到了嬰兒。

en: n. money that someone receives as payment for loss, damage or an injury; salary or pay for work; something that balances a bad thing; an action that makes up for something
ex: The company paid compensation to the injured workers.
公司對受傷的工人支付了賠償金。

en: n. a long structure that goes out into the water from the shore, used for boats to tie up; a structure that supports a bridge; a solid support for an arch or wall; a platform for fishing
ex: We walked to the end of the pier to watch the sunset.
我們走到碼頭盡頭看日落。

en: a. not making a profit; of an organization that uses its income to support its goals, not to make money for its owners; n. an organization that does not aim to make a profit
ex: She works for a nonprofit organization that helps the homeless.
她在一個幫助遊民的非營利組織工作。

en: a. happening too early or before the proper time; (of a baby) born before it is fully developed; made too soon without enough thought; n. a baby born early
ex: It is premature to draw any conclusions at this stage.
現階段下任何結論都還太早。

en: n. the large glass window at the front of a car; a transparent screen that protects people from the wind; (British: windscreen)
ex: The driver cleaned the windshield with a cloth.
司機用布擦拭擋風玻璃。

en: n. a combination of three or more musical notes played together; a straight line joining two points on a curve; (old use) a string on a musical instrument; a feeling that is expressed strongly
ex: The guitarist played a simple chord.
吉他手彈了一個簡單的和弦。

en: n. a large area of land with a large house on it; all the money and property that someone leaves when they die; a housing development; a stage or period of life
ex: He inherited a large estate from his grandfather.
他從祖父那裡繼承了一大片莊園。

en: n. a very small piece of something; a very small part of matter such as an atom or electron; a small word that does not change its form; a minute amount of something
ex: Tiny particles of dust floated in the sunlight.
細小的灰塵粒子在陽光中漂浮。

en: n. a general agreement among all the people in a group; a general opinion shared by most people; a decision that everyone accepts
ex: The committee reached a consensus after a long discussion.
委員會經過長時間討論後達成共識。

en: n. the back part of something; the area behind someone or something; a. at the back; vt. to look after children until they are grown up; to raise animals; to lift something up; vi. (of a horse) to stand on its back legs
ex: The children sat in the rear seat of the car.
孩子們坐在車子的後座。
